title: Nationwide Ground Stop Lifted, Nvidia Spy Scandal, Starship’s Longest Test Flight
summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Former UK Prime Minister and “Ending Alzheimer’s” Podcast Host David Cameron, Space Network Co-Founder Ross Hamilton, Axios Tech Policy Reporter Maria Curi, The Jamestown Foundation President and “Chinese Communist Espionage” Author and Former CIA Counterintelligence Analyst Peter Mattis, Poppi Co-Founder and Chief Brand Officer Allison Ellsworth and Poppi Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer Stephen Ellsworth. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pointed! Bloomberg’s Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
summary: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Entrepreneurs Behind Poppi Start Over
summary: Poppi founders Allison and Stephen Ellsworth tell Bloomberg This Weekend how they turned a farmers market business into a nearly $2 billion beverage brand and what they learned from the decade-long journey. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, the couple explains why they are starting over with Jetty, a new hydration brand, and how lessons about social media, hiring and building a team are shaping their second act. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How China’s Intelligence Operations Target Tech
summary: Former CIA counterintelligence analyst Peter Mattis tells Bloomberg This Weekend how China’s Ministry of State Security can use business and personal relationships to gather intelligence and potentially influence decision-making in strategically important industries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mattis explains why technology executives can become valuable targets even without access to classified information and how AI is expanding the capabilities of Chinese intelligence operations. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Stadium Bidding War Shaking Up the Midwest
summary: The Chicago Bears are weighing three possible homes for a new stadium: downtown Chicago, suburban Arlington Heights and Hammond, Indiana. The competition has turned into a high-stakes economic development battle involving billions of dollars in potential investment, tax incentives and public financing. Supporters say a new stadium could generate jobs, development and tax revenue, but former Indiana Governor Mitch Daniels warns that emotion can push politicians into deals that leave taxpayers paying the bill long after the ribbon cutting. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SpaceX Pushes Starship Reusability to New Test
summary: Space Network co-founder Ross Hamilton tells Bloomberg This Weekend why SpaceX’s attempt to catch Starship after its return from orbit could mark a major step toward making the rocket system fully reusable. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Hamilton explains how more frequent and less expensive launches could accelerate Starlink expansion, orbital data centers and SpaceX’s broader ambitions in space. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bessent, Lutnick Clash Over Nvidia China Curbs
summary: Axios AI policy reporter Maria Curi tells Bloomberg This Weekend about tensions inside the Trump administration over efforts to restrict the flow of advanced Nvidia chips to China and scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s handling of Megaspeed. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Curi explains the reported disagreements between Lutnick and other senior officials, including Scott Bessent, and the national security questions surrounding US technology exports to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Heads to China for Talks With Xi and Putin
summary: Bloomberg White House correspondent Jeff Mason tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the Trump administration responded to a nationwide FAA ground stop and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s push for $50 billion to modernize the US air traffic control system. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mason also looks ahead to President Donald Trump’s Asia trip and a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as technology and AI remain in focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SpaceX’s S&P 500 Bid Gets New Life as Musk Pitches Tesla Merger
summary: Just months after SpaceX was denied a swift entry into the S&P 500 Index, Elon Musk may have found a backdoor: Merging with Tesla Inc., one of the stock-market benchmark’s biggest members.

title: David Cameron Sees Hope in Alzheimer’s Research
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, former UK Prime Minister David Cameron discusses the personal toll of losing his mother to Alzheimer’s and the accelerating search for better diagnostics, treatments and ultimately a cure. Cameron tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini about promising drug research, the potential of blood tests to transform diagnosis and why governments should move faster to support clinical trials and expand access to new treatments. Cameron’s Ending Alzheimer’s podcast launches November 16. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ukraine Peace Push Turns to NATO and Donbas
summary: Bloomberg Economics defense lead Becca Wasser tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a US proposal linking NATO membership to Ukrainian concessions in the Donbas represents movement in peace talks but faces significant political and security hurdles. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Wasser also examines Ukraine’s battlefield pressures and how the US could reshape its military presence in the Middle East after the war with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Air Travel Chaos Puts FAA Systems in Focus
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence senior airlines analyst George Ferguson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nationwide ground stop underscores the difficulty of modernizing an aging US air traffic control system while keeping flights moving safely. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ferguson explains why upgrading legacy technology is so complicated and how airlines face the challenge of restoring schedules after thousands of cancellations and delays. (Source: Bloomberg)
